title: American put on a binomial tree
statement: Price an American put with a Cox–Ross–Rubinstein tree of n steps: u = e^{σ√Δt}, d = 1/u, risk-neutral p = (e^{rΔt} − d)/(u − d). At every node the value is max(continuation, immediate exercise K − S). Return the root value (absolute error ≤ 10⁻⁶).
hints: Terminal payoffs at the leaves, then step backwards: discounted risk-neutral expectation.
At each node compare with exercising now; keep one array of size n + 1.

solution.explanation: Backward induction (Part 13.3's optimal stopping) on a recombining tree: value = max(exercise now, e^{−rΔt}[p V_up + (1 − p) V_down]). American puts on non-dividend stocks are worth more than European ones when deep in the money and rates are positive, because receiving K early earns interest. American calls on non-dividend stocks are never exercised early (worth exactly the European price). The test (36, 40, 1, 0.06, 0.2) is the classic Longstaff–Schwartz benchmark, ≈ 4.48.
solution.python:
def american_put(S, K, T, r, sigma, n):
    from math import exp, sqrt
    dt = T / n; u = exp(sigma * sqrt(dt)); d = 1 / u; p = (exp(r * dt) - d) / (u - d); disc = exp(-r * dt)
    v = [max(K - S * u**j * d**(n - j), 0.0) for j in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        v = [max(disc * (p * v[j + 1] + (1 - p) * v[j]), K - S * u**j * d**(i - j)) for j in range(i + 1)]
    return v[0]
